question.text: Per Chapter 9, distressed debt financing for a going-concern company typically carries the following risk-return and structural characteristics:

answer.text: Lower coupon than performing companies; unsecured; no collateral requirement.
Always a minority equity investment, not debt.
Always convertible into equity at par value.
Higher cost than what a performing company may get; usually senior loans with adequate collateral; may also take form of preferred capital or structured off-balance-sheet debt.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Usually such financing are provided as senior loans with adequate collaterals and at a higher cost than what a performing company may get. Distress financing could also take the form of preferred capital or structured off-balance sheet debt.' The Trap: Option A inverts cost and collateral. Options C and D contradict the 'debt' nature of distress financing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A covers distressed-debt product feature. XV covers distressed-debt fair value. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use 'covenant headroom' (actual vs threshold) rather than just covenant-compliance tick-boxes. A distressed borrower running at 1.05x DSCR is a different risk than one at 1.5x, even if both are 'compliant'.
